answers.children: Rottweilers are moderately good with children because their large powerful build and protective guarding heritage make them watchful around small family members. Their history as livestock herders gives steady tolerance when they view youngsters as part of their charge, though their size can accidentally knock over toddlers during movement. The breed bonds intensely with household members and often acts as a living shield beside them. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Rottweilers can get along with other pets when raised together but their protective instincts and low stranger-friendly nature create tension with unfamiliar animals. Bred for guarding livestock their aloofness extends to same-sex dogs and they may assert dominance. With family cats or dogs they form steady bonds yet require clear leadership to prevent conflict.
answers.exercise: Rottweilers need one to two hours of daily exercise split between brisk walks, hikes and mental tasks such as tug-of-war. Their muscular build from herding and guarding work means they maintain endurance without high drive yet a bored Rottweiler becomes destructive chewing doorframes and testing boundaries. Purposeful activity keeps their confident temperament balanced.
answers.shedding: Yes — Rottweilers shed moderately with a short double coat that releases undercoat seasonally. The dense texture traps hair on furniture and clothing while the short length makes it easy to spot but harder to remove from carpets. Their working heritage produced a coat that needs minimal attention yet still demands regular vacuuming in the home.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic and the Rottweiler is not one commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Its short double coat sheds dander along with hair which can trigger reactions in sensitive people. The breed's protective build and guarding background offer no relief from the proteins that cling to its dense undercoat.
answers.training: Rottweilers are not easy for novices to train because their high intelligence combines with confident stubbornness that tests weak leadership. Bred for independent guarding and herding they respond well to consistent owners who channel their trainability into purposeful work yet their protective instincts make them aloof during sessions with strangers.
answers.lifespan: Rottweilers live 8-10 years. Their large muscular build from centuries of droving and guarding work contributes to the shorter range while the profile notes serious health issues that often require costly care. The breed's strength and endurance do not extend its years beyond this span.
answers.size: Adult Rottweilers reach 80-135 lb and stand 22-27 in at the shoulder. Their massive muscular frames create an imposing presence that feels like sharing space with a solid guardian who leans for affection or stands statue-still in protection. The substantial build from herding livestock makes them a heavy powerful companion indoors.
answers.barking: Rottweilers do not bark excessively because their guarding heritage favours low growls and alert posture over constant noise. They rumble at strangers approaching the door or property reflecting their role protecting butchers' earnings and livestock. The confident temperament keeps vocalisations purposeful rather than frequent.
answers.apartment: Rottweilers can live in an apartment if given sufficient daily exercise and mental structure. Their moderate energy and ability to settle calmly indoors suit smaller homes yet their protective instincts produce rumbling alerts at noises which may disturb neighbours. The powerful build demands space to move without knocking items over.
answers.first-time: Rottweilers are not a good first dog because their protective instincts and potential for aloof aggression with strangers demand an experienced owner who provides consistent leadership. The breed's intelligence and loyalty shine only with someone who meets their need for purpose otherwise the stubborn guarding traits create challenges.
